disagreements.researcher_position: Section 13 was last amended in 1982, so the consolidated corpus text of section 13(1) is the text in force at the April 2018 reference date, and the schedule requirements are the district, the village/pattu/korale or other division, and, for land in a town, the street name.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 13(1) was repealed and substituted by Act No. 48 of 2011, s.2, in force at the reference date. The list is wider: District, Pattu, Korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division, Grama Niladari Division and village, and for land in a municipality, town or developed area the number as well as the street name. The corpus edition of the principal Ordinance is a 1990 consolidation, which is why the 2011 substitution is not reflected in it; the amending Act is in the corpus and section 13 shows latest_change_year 1982, which is what led the researcher astray.

disagreements.researcher_position: The corpus does not expose the wording of Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (16) as it stood in April 2018, so the rule is supporting only and not applicable to the matter date.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus does expose it. Act No. 47 of 2011, s.2 substituted paragraph (a) of rule (16) and its as-enacted text is in the corpus; the next changes to section 31 are 2022 and 2024. Paragraph (a) as at April 2018 is therefore available. Only paragraph (b), which the 2011 Act did not touch, remains unconfirmable for the reference date.

disagreements.researcher_position: Section 13(7) requires a reference to the volume and folio of an earlier instrument relating to the same land to be written at the head of the deed presented for registration.
disagreements.verifier_position: The duty is conditional. The corpus body continues 'if such reference is known to the notary who prepared the instrument, or, if the instrument was not prepared by a notary, if such reference is known to the person presenting the instrument for registration'. The excerpt was cut before the condition, and claims CL-M107-Q04-006 and CL-M107-Q04-013 state the duty unconditionally.

unsupported_claims: CL-M107-Q04-001 (rejected): states the pre-2011 section 13(1) list as the requirement at the April 2018 reference date; superseded by 48-2011/s2.
CL-M107-Q04-006 (disputed): states the section 13(7) volume-and-folio duty without the statutory condition that the reference be known to the notary or to the person presenting the instrument.

CL-M107-Q04-009 (disputed): says the schedule must give the street name, the district and the division of the district; under the 2011 text it must also specify the Divisional Secretary's Division, the local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division, and, the land being in a town, the number.

CL-M107-Q04-012 (disputed): concludes that the drafted schedule states the particulars required by section 13(1) and 13(2); measured against the 2011 text it carries no assessment number for Lot C4, and the administrative divisions it does carry were taken from the notarial rule rather than from section 13.
CL-M107-Q04-013 (disputed): repeats the unconditional reading of section 13(7).
temporal_issues: Section 13(1): the map relies on the 1990-consolidation wording; the operative text at April 2018 is the substitution by Act No. 48 of 2011, s.2. This is the material defect in the matter.
Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (16)(a): the map relies on the post-2022 consolidation and records the 2018 wording as unavailable; it is available at 47-2011/s2.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (16)(b): genuinely unconfirmable for April 2018, because the corpus cannot attribute the 2022 and 2024 events on section 31 to particular paragraphs. Left supporting and not applicable to the matter date.

Sections 3, 7, 8 and 14 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance: no post-1982 amendment in the corpus touches them; 18-2024/s2 amends section 8 but postdates the reference date. Their temporal notes hold.
